description: The Moon at an instant or as a daily series: phase name and angle, illuminated fraction, distance, apparent size, libration, bright limb, and the next quarter phases. A location adds rise/set and altitude. For a calendar of new and full moons use astro_moon_phases; for the Moon's exact coordinates use astro_positions.

count.description: Number of daily rows from start (alternative to end).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous result's next_cursor. Send it with the same start/end arguments as the first page.

date.description: ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

end.description: Last day of a daily series. ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, north positive. Send lat and lon together.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, east positive (Lisbon is about -9.14). Send lat and lon together.

place.description: Place name instead of lat/lon, as "City" or "City,CC" with an ISO country code, e.g. "Lisbon,PT". Resolved server-side; the response then carries a required GeoNames CC BY 4.0 credit in its attribution field, which must be preserved when shown.

start.description: First day of a daily series. ISO 8601 UTC date or datetime, e.g. "2026-08-06" or "2026-08-06T21:00:00Z". Or jd: followed by a Julian Day on the UT scale, e.g. "jd:2461000.5". On astro_positions, date may list up to 24 datetimes separated by commas, answered in the order sent. Omit for the current moment. Years 1700 to 2200 only; outside that range the API refuses with DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE because the ephemeris is not reliable there.

tz.description: IANA timezone like "Europe/Lisbon" to render event times in local time. Optional; a resolved place supplies its own timezone.

name: astro_moon

outputSchema.description: The MCP projection of a CycleCalcs v2 response: the answer, plus the provenance a caller needs to use it honestly.

attribution.description: The credit line to display verbatim when rights is attribution_required.

data.description: The Moon's state and appearance, or a sampled series in range mode.

bright_limb.description: Which way the lit edge points.

constellation.description: The IAU constellation the Moon currently occupies.

distance_au.description: The same distance in astronomical units.

distance_basis.description: Whether the distance is geocentric or topocentric.

event_definition.description: The altitude convention rise and set are measured against.

fraction_of_mean_distance.description: Distance relative to the mean, for supermoon claims.

libration.description: The rocking that reveals a little of the far side.

next_phases.description: Upcoming quarter phases with exact instants.

parallax_deg.description: Angular shift between those two viewpoints.

phase.description: Phase name, angle and illuminated fraction.

position_geocentric.description: Position as seen from Earth's center.

position_topocentric.description: Position as seen from the given location.

rise_set.description: Moonrise and moonset for the location.

series.description: RANGE MODE ONLY: one sampled entry per step.

summary.description: A one-line reading of the Moon right now.

tropical_sign.description: Tropical ecliptic longitude, reported as position only.

window.description: The instant or range actually evaluated.

next_cursor.description: Present only when more rows exist. Send it back with the SAME start/end arguments as the first call to get the next page.

not_computed.description: Data this API deliberately does not serve, and why. Present only when the question touched such a field. An absence named here is information: treat it as "withheld", never as "none exists".

rights.description: Either unrestricted, or attribution_required when third-party place data was used. When attribution_required, the attribution line must be shown.

warnings.description: Machine-readable notices about this answer. Present only when non-empty. Never changes whether the call succeeded.

title: Moon state and appearance
